description:
FILED s536f (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08), the residue of #4323 (scratch/s536f/p/m4.pl rows 5, 13, 15 in the s536f worktree).  PRE-EXISTING: main c8886b61 answers the same.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    my $x = "x"; for (scalar($x)) { $_ .= "F" } print "1 $x\n";
    my $u = "u"; my $ref = \scalar($u); $$ref .= "R"; print "2 $u\n";
    my $m = "m"; map { $_ .= "X" } scalar($m); print "3 $m\n";

perl: `1 xF` / `2 uR` / `3 mX`.   PCL: `1 x` / `2 u` / `3 m`.

WHY (read): perl's scalar() returns the operand's SV, so `scalar(SCALAR)` is the scalar itself in every slot.  s536f routed the three ARGUMENT slots (named / method / coderef user calls) through `Pl::ExprToCL::_scalar_noop_operand`, so they lower the operand exactly as the bare argument; every other slot still lowers `(p-scalar E)`, a value.  The foreach list is decided on PPI tokens (`Pl::Parser::_foreach_single_scalar_p` / `_foreach_alias_rewrite` + VarAnnotator's veto `_ev_foreach_alias_list`), so it needs the same unwrap at the token level; `\` and map's list are ExprToCL slots that could ask the same helper.  A general rewrite `scalar(SCALAR) -> SCALAR` everywhere is exact in perl's semantics but moves every value-context `(p-scalar $x)` in the corpus (a tied scalar's FETCH moves to the consumer) -- measure first.


=== DONE (s536i) ===
`scalar(E)` of a scalar place in a foreach / map / grep list is E as one slot (%p-aliasing-slice-form's p-scalar arm, %p-scalar-alias-form): a variable, a scalar deref (p-cast-$-box), and an ELEMENT as its LAZY -argbox cell -- perl creates nothing for `for (scalar($h{zz})) {}` and creates the key on a write (probed; an eager first version vivified).  `\scalar(E)` is `\E`: every `\` spelling goes through ExprToCL::_backslash_lvalue_form, which asks _scalar_noop_operand (the inline prefix-`\` copy is gone); `\scalar($h{z})` creates the key as `\$h{z}` does (probed).  The foreach slot walk goes into `scalar(...)`; the map / grep walk too.  Guard Pl/t/proto-alias-01.t row 12 (a tied scalar FETCH 1 / STORE 1; fails on 3139fcb0).  Commit: subject `s536i WIP #4685`.  Residue: the PARENTHESISED one-element `\(scalar($x))` / `\(scalar($a[0]))` still references a copy = #4783 (filed by the s538 pre-review, pre-existing on main).
